title: RevocationChecker default skip is a pit of failure for custom impls
description: RevocationChecker::check_revocation_against_anchor has a default impl that returns Ok(()) (skip). The trait rustdoc (pkix-revocation/src/lib.rs lines 615-703) warns about this extensively, and pkix-chain's verify_chain rustdoc (pkix-chain/src/lib.rs lines 367-383) documents it again. But the API shape itself is a pit of failure: any custom RevocationChecker that only implements check_revocation() will silently skip the anchor-issued cert with no compile-time or runtime signal. The warning text is thorough, but the damage when someone misses it is a silent security gap (the cert closest to the root is unchecked). What goes wrong: a consumer implements RevocationChecker with only check_revocation(), deploys it, and the cert issued directly by the trust anchor is never revocation-checked. There is no test assertion, no log, no metric — just a silent Ok(()). Consider: (a) a lint or clippy-style check in CI that detects impl RevocationChecker without check_revocation_against_anchor, (b) a sealed helper trait that requires both methods, or (c) a runtime diagnostic on the Verifier that logs when the default is hit. This is an API-contract risk, not a correctness bug in the existing code — CrlChecker and OcspChecker both override correctly.
